svg.title: Articles & persuasion
svg.desc: Headline & opening: Use a headline that reveals the angle. Begin with a relevant moment, contrast or focused question. Reach the subject quickly. A long fictional story can take over an article. Write for these readers: School magazine: familiar situations and a lively, respectful voice. Formal publication: adapt the register. Direct address can involve readers. Avoid blaming them or assuming everyone has the same life. Develop paragraphs: One main idea → concrete example → why it matters. Change paragraph when the job or focus changes. Connect naturally: “This small change ...”, “Another difficulty ...”, “That benefit ...”. Use devices deliberately: A question sharpens an issue; a contrast clarifies a choice; a three-part pattern gives rhythm. Reasons support persuasion. Techniques express them. Do not force every device into every piece. Handle a real objection: Concede → respond → justify. Accept a valid concern and give a workable answer. “After-school travel is difficult; a lunchtime trial offers another route.” Avoid dismissing opponents. A purposeful close: Bring the message together. Return to an opening image or give a practical next step. “Choose one room, one lunchtime and one chance.” Do not introduce a major new argument at the end.
